instruction.text: Drag the indicator words to the tenses they are usually used with.
Fill in the gap with the correct verb.

atoms.b: Elephants ((++have has had)) big, floppy ears.

wrong.text: Elephants 'always' have big, floppy ears, so you have to use present tense.

atoms.b: We ((have has ++had)) a wonderful week in Italy last summer.

wrong.text: 'Last summer' shows that the action has already happened, so you have to use past tense.

atoms.b: Yesterday, we ((have has ++had)) dinner in an Indian restaurant.

wrong.text: 'Yesterday' shows that the action has already happened, so you have to use past tense.

atoms.b: Her old car was blue. Now she ((have ++has had)) a green car.

wrong.text: 'Now' shows that the action is currently happening, so you have to use the present tense.

atoms.b: They ((have has ++had)) a good time at the fair last week.

wrong.text: 'Last week' shows that the action has already happened, so you have to use past tense.

atoms.b: They ((++have has had)) two kids now.

wrong.text: 'Now' shows that the action is currently happening, so you have to use the present tense.
